messages:
maria: Quick question — legal needs an 'operator justification' artifact before we adjust RBAC for the BYOK HSM sidecar. Specifically: what is the absolute-minimum operator privilege set we can grant, what audit records must we produce, and what phrasing satisfies SOC2/PCI reviewers?

devon: Short answer: JIT + least-privilege + signed audit records.
Minimal roles I usually propose: hsm.session.manage, hsm.key.wrap, hsm.key.unwrap, hsm.metrics.read. No long-lived full-admin.
Example RBAC role (keep it narrow):
```yaml
name: hsm-byo-operator-limited
permissions:
  - hsm.session.create
  - hsm.session.close
  - hsm.key.wrap
  - hsm.metrics.read
notes: "Scoped to customer tenant and single physical HSM cluster"
```
Also require justification doc + manager attestation for each operator.

ashwin: Audit + compliance side: centralize signed operator session logs to our SIEM; include operator identity, session id, commands executed (diff output), and key identifiers (no key material). Retention: SOC2 generally expects reasonable retention (90–365d), PCI can require longer for some artifacts — check control mapping, but for key custody evidence we often keep 7 years for legal holds.
On KMS integration: always store wrapped key blobs in our metadata store and record CMK ARN/hash used for wrapping. Rewrap cadence: default 90 days for high-risk customers, configurable.

kevin: For emergency access / break-glass: multi-party approval + short-lived escalation tokens. Proposed runbook (brief):
- Incident declared by SRE/Customer Security.
- Pager duty notifies 2-of-3 approvers.
- Approver runs JIT grant (valid 15m) and records rationale in ticket.
- Operator performs operation; session is recorded & signed.
- Post-mortem within 48h, rotate any wrapped keys used.
We should also require HSM-level unseal to be M-of-N and log that event.

oncall-bot: [alert] New doc request logged: #DOC-4350011122 — Security will own operator-justification template.

maria: Thanks — does anyone have a one-file checklist I can hand Legal (RBAC lines + audit artifacts + sample justification text)? I want to avoid back-and-forth.

devon: Paste for Legal checklist (one-liner bullet form):
- Operator role: list allowed APIs (see RBAC snippet).
- Access model: JIT + MFA + short TTL (<=15m).
- Approval: manager attestation + 2nd approver for break-glass.
- Audit: signed session id, command transcript, wrapped-key IDs, CMK reference, SIEM index name.
- Retention: X days (customer tier configurable) + keep hashes for >=7y for legal cases.
- Controls: M-of-N unseal + periodic rewrap (90d default).
Sample justification text (one paragraph):
"Operator X requires scoped BYOK operator privileges to perform wrapped-key maintenance and emergency unseal actions for tenant Y. Access will be JIT-provisioned, time-limited, approved by two managers for break-glass, and fully recorded with signed session traces forwarded to our SIEM under index 'hsm-ops'."

ashwin: A couple vuln-triage notes to add to the checklist:
- If firmware vuln found: immediately freeze operator creds, disable non-essential operator APIs, notify affected tenants, trigger key-rotation plan (prioritize rewrap/derive flow if available).
- Capture vendor advisory, CVE id, and affected HSM serials in the incident ticket.
- If we used KMS-wrapping, we can often rewrap without exposing raw key material — include that as mitigation step.

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll draft the actual template and put it in /docs/sec/playbooks/byok-operator-justification.md Monday. Any objections to recommending 90-day default rewrap for tier-1?

maria: No objections from Legal side. Tagging @ashwin to own the template language and @devon to add the RBAC snippets.

ashwin: I can own wording — will include mapping to SOC2 sections and PCI key custody notes. Will add SIEM field mapping example: hsm.session.id => hsm.session_id, operator => user.email, command => hsm.command_text, wrappedKeyId => hsm.wrapped_key_id.

maria: Awesome — thanks all. I'll reference this thread in the legal ticket.
